tasks.title: Five @unchecked Sendable declarations, none with a written justification
tasks.evidence_before: git grep '@unchecked Sendable' -- Sources => DocumentIngestor, HTTPServer, EventStream, ProgressBox
tasks.fix_summary: Every @unchecked Sendable conformance in Sources/ now carries a doc comment stating the invariant the compiler cannot check, naming the lock or actor each piece of mutable state is confined to, and saying what keeps that true: HTTPServer (connections/streams/running/failure under stateLock), EventStream (private `open` under `lock`), ProgressBox (private `lastReported` under `lock`, callback after unlock), ToolRegistry (private `tools` under `lock`, ToolProvider: Sendable makes the escape safe), DocumentIngestor (no `var` at all, so `let` immutability is the whole of the confinement). Doc comments only; no code changed.
tasks.evidence_after: grep -rn '@unchecked Sendable' Sources/ | grep -v comment => 5 declarations (HTTPServer.swift:242,268; MLXEngine.swift:797,822; Attachments.swift:274), each immediately preceded by a justification that names the lock. swift build => Build complete, 0 warnings 0 errors. swift test => Test run with 557 tests in 77 suites passed.
tasks.notes: The ledger enumerated four sites; a fifth, ToolRegistry (MLXEngine.swift), post-dates that enumeration and was found by grep during the fix. The required outcome is 'every conformance in Sources/', so it was justified as well - the enumeration being short is recorded here rather than quietly absorbed. Each type was read for a genuinely broken invariant, not just annotated: no real race was found, so no new task. The forced test-target rebuild showed 8 unique warning sites under Tests/, not the 5 the baseline recorded - the baseline file was produced by a grep that mangled multi-line diagnostics. A03 must therefore fix 8, not 5; recorded against A03.

tasks.title: WebTransport is pinned by range while the project has twice depended on an exact transport behaviour
tasks.evidence_before: Package.swift 'from: "1.3.7"'; the 1.3.7 floor exists because 1.3.6 had a lifetime connection cap
tasks.fix_summary: The WebTransport dependency is pinned exactly (Package.swift:47) with a comment stating why: the transport is the security boundary for the engine connection, and two behaviours this app depends on are tied to its exact version - the newConnectionLimit lifetime-cap semantics changed in 1.3.7, and the first-frame subscription trigger documented in WebTransportClient.connect(). No other dependency touched.
tasks.evidence_after: swift package resolve => exit 0, 0 warnings; Package.resolved unchanged, webtransport version 1.3.7 revision 3df28f2a. swift build => 0 warnings 0 errors. swift test => 557 tests in 77 suites passed.
tasks.notes: Deviation, stated rather than hidden: the literal `.exact("1.3.7")` spelling is deprecated under swift-tools-version 6.3 and emits a manifest warning. Suppressing a warning is forbidden, so the non-deprecated labelled form `exact: "1.3.7"` (package(url:exact:)) was used - the same exact requirement, warning-free. Verified independently by the coordinator: the manifest builds with 0 warnings and resolves to 1.3.7.

tasks.title: AddressSanitizer over the whole suite: clean
tasks.evidence_before: no sanitizer baseline exists; ASan attempt in flight at baseline/swift-test-asan.log
tasks.fix_summary: no fix needed — the instrumented run is the deliverable
tasks.evidence_after: swift test --sanitize=address --scratch-path ~/Library/Caches/ChatBots/audit-asan => exit 0, 555 tests in 77 suites passed, no AddressSanitizer report anywhere in the log

tasks.title: ThreadSanitizer over the whole suite: one data race found
tasks.evidence_before: not run
tasks.fix_summary: no fix here — the finding is opened as A14
tasks.evidence_after: swift test --sanitize=thread --scratch-path ~/Library/Caches/ChatBots/audit-tsan => TSAN_EXIT=1, 555 tests passed, ThreadSanitizer: reported 1 warnings, SUMMARY: data race HTTPServer.swift:356 in closure #2 in HTTPServer.start()
tasks.notes: The suite still passed — which is why the run matters. Expected clean; it was not.

tasks.title: isRunning/lastError are raced between the listener callback and waitUntilReady
tasks.evidence_before: TSan: Write of size 1 at HTTPServer.swift:356 (closure #2 in start(), GCD worker) vs Previous read at HTTPServer.swift:380 (waitUntilReady, concurrency thread); block allocated by APIServer.start() APIServer.swift:350
tasks.fix_summary: isRunning/lastError moved behind stateLock: private stored flags with markRunning()/markStopped() writers and lock-guarded computed accessors; the class doc now carries a true invariant instead of an assertion
tasks.evidence_after: swift test --sanitize=thread --scratch-path ~/Library/Caches/ChatBots/audit-tsan => TSAN_AFTER_EXIT=0, 555 tests passed, no ThreadSanitizer report (baseline/swift-test-tsan-after.log); plain swift test: 555 pass
tasks.notes: The race is only observable under the instrument, so the failing-then-passing evidence is the TSan pair rather than a unit assertion. A17 was found while fixing this and shares the commit: same class, same conformance, same invariant.

tasks.title: Attaching a document blocks the engine main actor for the whole conversion, subprocess wait included
tasks.evidence_before: DocumentIngestorProvider.ingestor.add is synchronous; DocumentImport.swift:163-166 polls usleep(20000) to a deadline; EngineService is @MainActor and calls it from addAttachment (EngineService.swift:325-357), so the actor every front end and the transport share is blocked
tasks.notes: S1 not S2: the blocked actor is shared, so the failure is an unresponsive app, not a slow conversion. Moving it off the actor depends on settling A05 for DocumentIngestor.

tasks.title: --serve has no signal handling, so the listener is never shut down and nothing is flushed on exit
tasks.evidence_before: main.swift:689 while true { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3600)) } with no SIGINT/SIGTERM handler; WebTransportEngineServer.stop() and HTTP teardown never run
tasks.notes: No data loss — ConversationStore writes per turn — but the port is never released and logs are not flushed.

tasks.title: streams is appended on the main actor without the lock that every other access takes
tasks.discovered_by: found while fixing A14 (review beside the TSan report)
tasks.evidence_before: stop(), closeStreams() and finish() all mutate streams under stateLock; the append in the SSE path ran on @MainActor carrying the comment that streams is only ever touched on the main actor, which was never true because finish() runs on the network queue
tasks.fix_summary: addStream(_:) takes stateLock and is the only append; the false comment replaced with the reason
tasks.evidence_after: swift test 555 pass; swift test --sanitize=thread exit 0 (baseline/swift-test-tsan-after.log)
tasks.notes: A concurrent append against a locked mutation of a Swift array is memory unsafety, not a stale value, so S1. Shares A14's commit deliberately: same class, same conformance, same invariant; splitting would have committed a knowingly half-fixed type.

tasks.title: The suite is not hermetic: three tests need the developer's private models/ and .secrets.env and fail on a fresh clone
tasks.evidence_before: node1 fresh clone of audit/2026-09-13: build exit 0, test exit 1, 4 issues in 3 tests - BuiltInKeys.deepSeek nil (no .secrets.env) and ModelStore.declaresVision nil for the default checkpoint (no models/). BuiltInKeyTests.swift:18 says the test skips when the file is absent, but try #require throws, so it fails.
tasks.fix_summary: The three machine-local assertions are now .enabled(if:) gated on the state they actually need - a DeepSeek key for BuiltInKeyTests.deepSeekGetsTheKey, and an on-disk default checkpoint for ImageUploadTests.localCheckpointSees and AttachmentTests.localCheckpoint - so a fresh clone skips them instead of failing. The logic they were standing in for is covered hermetically instead: AttachmentTests now writes synthetic checkpoints into a temporary models root and asserts that a config declaring a vision_config reads as true, a text-only config reads as a definite false, and an absent model reads as nil (unknown). Coverage of the rule went up; the suite no longer depends on 3 GB of weights or a private key.
tasks.evidence_after: node1 (independent host, fresh clone of 518c38e, no models/, no .secrets.env): BUILD_EXIT=0, TEST_EXIT=0, 'Test run with 557 tests in 77 suites passed'. The three machine-local tests report exactly 'skipped.' rather than failing. Local: swift test 557 tests in 77 suites passed; with CHATBOTS_MODELS_DIR pointed at an empty directory the same run passes and the two vision tests report skipped, proving the gate is on the checkpoint and not on the host.
tasks.notes: Gate behaviour was checked in both directions rather than only on the happy path: local run with a checkpoint present executes the tests and passes; local run with CHATBOTS_MODELS_DIR aimed at an empty directory skips them and passes. The DeepSeek gate is keyed on key presence, so it still runs here (a key exists) and skipped on node1 (none does). Verified on node1 per the brief's requirement that a fresh clone be green on a host that did not develop the fix.

tasks.file_line: Sources/ChatBotsCore/HTTPServer.swift (named by 948ea29, which commits no source file)
tasks.title: A DONE task was committed with its evidence and its ledger entry but without its fix: 948ea29 claims A14 and A17 and contains no source change
tasks.discovered_by: Phase C re-entry: `git status` showed HTTPServer.swift modified on a tree whose ledger already said A14 and A17 were DONE
tasks.evidence_before: git show --name-only 948ea29 => AUDIT/baseline/swift-test-tsan-after.log, AUDIT/baseline/test-warnings.txt, AUDIT/ledger.json, AUDIT/ledger.json.tmp, AUDIT/ledger.md, AUDIT/plan.md; no file under Sources/. git show HEAD:Sources/ChatBotsCore/HTTPServer.swift | grep 'private var running' => no match, so the flags that commit message says are guarded by stateLock were still plain stored properties at HEAD. A 0-byte AUDIT/ledger.json.tmp was committed by the same accident.
tasks.fix_summary: The A14/A17 fix is committed for real on this branch (repair commit below), AUDIT/*.tmp is ignored so an interrupted ledger write cannot be committed again, and AUDIT/verify-done-commits.sh makes the claim mechanically checkable: it reads every DONE task, takes the source paths that task's own record names, and fails unless that task's commit touches one of them.
tasks.evidence_after: AUDIT/verify-done-commits.sh => exit 0, every DONE task backed; git show --stat of the repair commit lists Sources/ChatBotsCore/HTTPServer.swift; swift test 557 tests in 77 suites pass; swift test --sanitize=thread exit 0 with no report
tasks.notes: The sanitizer evidence in 948ea29 is genuine: the ThreadSanitizer re-run was done against a working tree with the fix applied, and baseline/swift-test-tsan-after.log shows zero race reports. What was missing was the code. This is the one failure mode where the ledger is not wrong about the result, only about where the result lives, so the guard is mechanical rather than a matter of care. The guard is deliberately narrow: a DONE task that names no source path (a CI file, a decision, a document) is reported as skipped, not as passed.

tasks.title: Stored DOM XSS: the live-pane header interpolates the moderator-supplied seat name into innerHTML
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: web/app.js createLiveElement built its header with `el.innerHTML = `${name.toUpperCase()}` ...`. `name` is the seat name from the server snapshot (called at web/app.js:470 and :485 with seat.name). POST /api/seat accepts an arbitrary name and the rename UI posts arbitrary contentEditable text, so a name of `` is stored and executes in every client that renders a live turn in that room. .toUpperCase() is not sanitisation: tag and attribute names are case-insensitive. Every other render path in the file escapes (bodyHTML, escapeHTML, labelFor/textContent), so this was an isolated miss. The same bytes ship in the generated WebAssets.swift.
tasks.fix_summary: web/app.js createLiveElement no longer interpolates the seat's name into innerHTML: the header scaffold is built as a fixed string and the name is assigned with textContent. `python3 tools/embed-web.py` regenerated Sources/ChatBotsCore/WebAssets.swift so the served bytes carry the fix, and a regression test reads the asset the server actually serves (not the file) and asserts the function sets the name as text and contains no `${name` interpolation. The test delimits the function by its closing brace rather than a character window, because the first version of the guard silently truncated the body and passed a string it had cut short - the same failure mode as the counts in A28.
tasks.evidence_after: swift build --build-tests => Build complete, 0 warnings 0 errors (under the new A03 warnings-as-errors gate); python3 tools/embed-web.py --check => exit 0; swift test => 558 tests in 77 suites passed, including 'The live header renders the seat's name as text, never as markup'. The guard was shown to fail first: with a 900-character window it failed on the fixed code because the comment pushed textContent out of the window, which is what prompted delimiting by the function's closing brace.
tasks.notes: The XSS is reachable by anyone who can reach the API, which per A01 is anyone on the LAN, so it is a stored, self-propagating script injection against every open browser rather than a self-XSS.

tasks.title: The model-download integrity check silently degrades to 'accept any size' when the HEAD request yields nothing
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: The per-file expected size is read with a HEAD request and recorded as `${size:-0}`. download_file then accepts any existing file when expected is 0 (`[ "$expected" = "0" ] || ...` at :211) and skips the post-download size check at :242. A truncated file, or an error body written by `curl -L -o` without `-f`, is recorded as a complete model. The comment beside it claims the size 'is what proves a download finished', so the integrity step becomes a no-op without saying so.
tasks.notes: Fails open, which is the wrong direction for an integrity check. The correct behaviour is to refuse to record a size of 0 as a pass.

tasks.title: stop_all kills a stale PID from a pid file without checking the process is ours
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: The pid-file branch runs a bare `kill -TERM "$pid"` after only `kill -0`. The command-name ownership check (`ps ... | grep -qE "chatbots|caddy"`) exists only in the by-port branch at :115. A pid file left behind by a crash plus OS PID reuse makes `start.sh --stop`, or the restart path at :215, SIGTERM an unrelated user process.
tasks.notes: The script already contains the correct check; it is simply not applied on this branch.

tasks.title: capture-devices.py prints a viewport mismatch but cannot fail the run
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: The comment claims both width and overflow are 'checked rather than assumed', but a requested-vs-actual viewport mismatch only prints (`print(f"    ! viewport {metrics['viewport']} != requested {requested_width}")`). Only failures/overflows/forced_failures set the exit code at :323. The docstring promises a non-zero exit on any failed capture, so a screenshot rendered at the wrong width is published under that device profile's name and the run stays green.
tasks.notes: Same class as A18 and A19: a stated guarantee the code does not implement, so nobody notices.

tasks.title: A native binary artifact is downloaded with no integrity check and embedded in the signed app
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: Cmlx.xcframework.zip is fetched from a GitHub release URL with only `curl -fL` - no digest, no signature - unzipped, and default.metallib is copied into the .app's Contents/MacOS at :101, where make-app.sh ad-hoc signs it. Unlike the model files in install.sh there is not even a size check. A compromised release, or a TLS-terminating proxy, yields arbitrary native code inside the shipped, signed application.
tasks.notes: Supply-chain exposure created by the audit scope's own §1 requirement that the toolchain be reproducible.

tasks.title: install.sh interpolates the project path into `bash -c`, so an apostrophe in the path is command injection
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: `bash -c "cd '$ROOT' && swift run -c release chatbots-cli --check"` pastes the project path inside single quotes inside a double-quoted command string. A path containing an apostrophe breaks the quoting: the transport and model checks fail with a shell syntax error, and a crafted directory name such as `...'; cmd; echo '` is command injection at install time. The launcher written to ~/Applications has the same flaw inside its single-quoted osascript string.
tasks.notes: Requires the user to install from an oddly-named directory, so S3 rather than S2 - but it is a genuine injection sink, not a quoting nit.

tasks.title: run_with_timeout kills the wrapper but not the process tree it timed out on
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: `"$@" &` backgrounds `bash -c "swift run ..."`; the timeout then kills that bash PID only. `swift run` and the built chatbots-cli are grandchildren and survive - precisely the GPU-holding child the timeout exists to stop. The installer reports that the check 'was stopped' while the process keeps occupying the GPU through the following steps and retries.

tasks.title: cdp.py stop() refuses to terminate any Chrome started with a non-default profile
tasks.discovered_by: Phase B, L3/L4 line-depth pass over tools/ and web/
tasks.evidence_before: `_is_our_headless_instance` hardcodes the profile marker "chatbots-cdp" instead of checking `self.profile` (the constructor parameter at :137). Any caller passing a custom --user-data-dir leaves a headless Chrome running, and the next start() rmtree's the profile directory and races for the same debugging port. capture-devices.py currently uses the default, so it is latent; its own TMP_PROFILE constant at :41 is dead code.
tasks.notes: Latent: no current caller triggers it. Recorded because the guard exists and does not guard.

tasks.title: Three recorded counts are wrong and the rest are not reproducible from the commands that produced them
tasks.discovered_by: Phase C re-entry, while re-deriving the baseline
tasks.evidence_before: Re-derived every recorded number against the tree. Wrong: shellcheck recorded as 24 notes is 7 findings (the baseline file is 24 lines and its line count was read as a finding count); the test target's warning sites recorded as 5 are 8 (the capturing grep truncated multi-line diagnostics); 'Force unwraps in Sources/: two', recorded as reviewed and clean, is 12 `!` sites. Not reproducible: swift-format '29 900 diagnostics' is the baseline file's line count, and an unscoped `swiftlint lint` also lints .build/checkouts and reports ~37 000 where the record says 401. Correct as recorded: ruff 11, pyright 2, semgrep 3, gitleaks 0, try? 72 sites across 23 files, ASan clean, TSan one race then clean.
tasks.notes: The errors run in both directions - the warning count was understated, the shellcheck count overstated, the force-unwrap review understated - so a reader cannot assume the error is conservative. The yardstick the whole audit measures against therefore needs a stated method per number, not just a number. The twelve `!` sites themselves are all currently unreachable traps and are part of this task's fix.
